source_text: VIII. Εἶτα δὲ Πιονίῳ εἶπεν Πολέμων· Πείσθητι ἡμῖν, Πιόνιε. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Κεκέλευσαι ἢ πείθειν ἢ κολάζειν· οὐ πείθεις, κόλαζε. Τότε ἐπερωτᾷ ὁ νεωκόρος Πολέμων λέγων· Ἐπίθυσον, Πιόνιε. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Ὅτι Χριστιανός εἰμι. Πολέμων εἶπεν· Ποῖον θεὸν σέβῃ; Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Τὸν θεὸν τὸν παντοκράτορα τὸν ποιήσαντα τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ πάντας ἡμᾶς, ὃς παρέχει ἡμῖν πάντα πλουσίως, ὃν ἐγνώκαμεν διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ. Πολέμων εἶπεν· Ἐπίθυσον οὖν κἂν τῷ αὐτοκράτορι. Πιόνιος εἶπεν· Ἐγὼ ἀνθρώπῳ οὐκ ἐπιθύω, Χριστιανὸς γάρ εἰμι.
pass_a_gloss: Next Polemon said to Pionius, 'Be persuaded by us, Pionius.' Pionius said, 'You have been ordered either to persuade or to punish; you do not persuade, punish.' Then Polemon the temple-warden asks him in turn, saying, 'Sacrifice, Pionius.' Pionius said, 'Because I am a Christian.' Polemon said, 'What god do you worship?' Pionius said, 'The all-ruling God who made heaven and earth and all things in them and all of us, who furnishes to us all things richly, whom we knew through his Word Christ.' Polemon said, 'Sacrifice therefore at least to the emperor.' Pionius said, 'I do not sacrifice to a man, for I am a Christian.'
pass_b_english: Then Polemon said to Pionius, “Let yourself be persuaded by us, Pionius.” Pionius said, “Your orders are either to persuade or to punish; since you are not persuading, punish.” Then Polemon the temple-warden put the question to him again, saying, “Offer sacrifice, Pionius.” Pionius said, “I am a Christian.” Polemon said, “What god do you worship?”

Pionius said, “God the Almighty, who made heaven and earth and all that is in them (Acts 4:24) and made all of us, who gives us all things richly (1 Timothy 6:17), whom we came to know through his Word, Christ.” Polemon said, “Then offer sacrifice at least to the emperor.” Pionius said, “I do not offer sacrifice to a human being, for I am a Christian.”
